stories.title: Workers are rewriting their LinkedIn histories to add AI skills. Here's what they're dropping.
stories.simple_summary: People are updating their job profiles on LinkedIn to highlight AI skills they've learned, while removing or downplaying other abilities from their resumes.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're job hunting or managing staff, knowing that AI skills are becoming more valued on resumes tells you what employers are looking for right now.

stories.title: AI bubble or babble? How to understand — and make money — on the latest tech revolution
stories.simple_summary: A news article discusses whether AI is a genuine opportunity or overhyped excitement, and suggests ways to potentially profit from it.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors looking to make money on AI trends — nothing you need to act on unless you're considering investing.

stories.title: Taiwan issues indictments over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
stories.simple_summary: Taiwan's government has charged some people with illegally selling AI computer servers (very powerful machines) to China, which the government wanted to prevent.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly a government and international trade issue — it doesn't affect your daily life or business.

stories.title: 'Don't ask me to print your ChatGPT birthday card': Hitting back at AI 'slop'
stories.simple_summary: Some people are annoyed that AI-generated content (called 'slop') is low-quality, and one person is refusing to use AI to create things like birthday cards because they want real, thoughtful work instead.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a sign that people want genuine, human-made things for personal moments — so handmade or personally written items may feel more valued.

stories.title: AI is coming for your glasses
stories.simple_summary: AI technology is being added to eyeglasses, though the article doesn't specify exactly what features these smart glasses will have.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly about technology companies developing new products — nothing you need to worry about or act on right now.

stories.title: Workers in China worry over being replaced as they adapt to the growing impact of AI on jobs
stories.simple_summary: Workers in China are worried that AI might take over their jobs as companies increasingly use these tools to do work that people used to do.
stories.why_it_matters: This reflects a real concern that exists worldwide — if you own a business, it's worth thinking about how AI tools might change your work, both as threats and opportunities.

stories.title: Dr. Dre Says He Uses AI to Produce Songs
stories.simple_summary: The musician Dr. Dre says he uses AI as a tool to help him produce songs.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows that professionals in creative fields are using AI as a helper tool rather than seeing it as only a threat to their work.

stories.title: Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha?
stories.simple_summary: A new AI tool called Ox Alpha has appeared mysteriously online, and people are guessing who created it and what it does.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mostly internet speculation and gossip — nothing practical for you to know about or use.

stories.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
stories.simple_summary: A company called Linkdaze made a free digital calendar that can help manage your household tasks and even plan meals using AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in digital tools to organize your home or family schedule, this is one free option to explore.

stories.title: Flock CEO calls for ‘compromise’ as surveillance company faces growing backlash
stories.simple_summary: Flock Safety is a company that sells surveillance technology to track people, and it's facing criticism from the public who worry it could be misused.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're concerned about privacy or surveillance in your town, this is a company whose practices are being questioned.

stories.title: Is it legal to train AI models on copyrighted books? It’s complicated
stories.simple_summary: Publishers and authors are unhappy because AI systems were trained using their copyrighted books without permission, and they're questioning whether this is legal.
stories.why_it_matters: If you write or create things, this shows the ongoing struggle between AI companies wanting to use existing work and creators wanting to protect their rights.

stories.title: Alibaba shares plunge after $10bn new share placement to fund AI spending
stories.simple_summary: The large company Alibaba announced it's spending $10 billion more on AI development, and this news caused its stock price to drop.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to stock investors — nothing you need to act on unless you own Alibaba shares.
